title: Integrated Security & Compliance Playbook: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, SDLC, Incident Response, Evidence & Exceptions
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

This consolidated playbook defines Redwood Inference’s standard controls, operational workflows, and evidence collection patterns for: RBAC and authentication, audit logging, data residency & retention, secure SDLC requirements, incident response security procedures, compliance evidence workflows, and risk/exception handling. The intent is to provide a single reference for engineering, security, and audit stakeholders to implement, operate, and evidence controls consistently across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments.

Table of contents
1. Scope and applicability
2. RBAC and authentication model
3. Audit logging architecture and SLOs
4. Data residency and retention rules
5. Secure SDLC requirements and gating
6. Incident response (security) procedures
7. Compliance evidence collection workflows
8. Risk and exception process
9. Ownership and escalation
10. Appendix: sample queries, commands, and templates

1. Scope and applicability
- Applies to all customer-facing services, admin tooling, CI/CD pipelines, control plane components, and private deployment artifacts maintained by Redwood Inference.
- Exceptions: ephemeral research experiments kept in isolated repos must follow an alternate documented process and sign-off (see section 8).

2. RBAC and authentication model
Intro: We enforce least-privilege via role-based access control (RBAC) backed by a centralized identity provider (IdP) and fine-grained service identities for machine-to-machine (M2M) auth.

Key components:
- Identity providers: Okta (corporate SSO) + SCIM for user provisioning; customer-managed IdP support for Dedicated/Private.
- Service accounts: short-lived mTLS or OIDC tokens issued by our auth-service.
- Authorization layer: policy engine (open-source Casbin v2.x pattern) in the authz gateway.

Standard roles and responsibilities (examples):
- role:admin-platform — Full platform admin (create/modify orgs, billing, infra). Owner: Platform Security.
- role:engineer-service — Deploy and operate a named service (read/write to service resources). Owner: Service Team.
- role:read-only-audit — Read-only access to operational dashboards and logs. Owner: Security.
- role:customer-admin — Customer-facing admin for Dedicated/Private tenants (scoped per-tenant only). Owner: Customer Success.

Controls and thresholds:
- All human interactive access requires MFA (Okta MFA enforced).
- Privileged role grants require two approvers and a documented business justification in Access Request tickets (Jira).
- Service account tokens expire <= 1 hour by default; long-lived credentials require rotation with KMS-backed key material and documented exception.

Provisioning & de-provisioning workflow (high level):
1) Access request created in Jira with owner and justification.
2) Two approvers from the owner_team approve.
3) SCIM provisioning (Okta) grants role.
4) Automated weekly entitlement review job emails owners for attestation (90-day remediation SLA).

Audit requirements for RBAC:
- Daily snapshot of role bindings exported to audit-bucket (encrypted) with checksum and retention 365 days for Hosted by default.
- Policy change events (create/update/delete role/policy) must be logged and retained per section 4.

3. Audit logging architecture and SLOs
Goals: Ensure reliable, tamper-evident capture of admin actions, API requests, model inference metadata (for billing/forensics), and infra-level events.

Architecture summary:
- Ingest: Services emit structured JSON logs to stdout and an in-process audit client that forwards to local agent (audit-collector).
- Transport: audit-collector batches and forwards to central pipeline (kafka/audit-topic) with at-least-once delivery.
- Storage: Immutable object store (S3-compatible) + index in Splunk/Elasticsearch for search.
- Integrity: Periodic Merkle-tree manifests and signed manifests using KMS keys to detect tampering.

SLOs and thresholds:
- Ingest latency (service -> central index searchable): P95 <= 60s, P99 <= 120s.
- Delivery success rate: >= 99.9% per day.
- Retention and durability: audit objects written with versioning + lifecycle rules to meet retention policy.

Log contents / required fields (structured JSON):
- timestamp, service, env, request_id, user_id / service_account, action, resource, outcome (success/failure), reason, request_payload_hash, response_hash, location (region), tenant_id (if applicable).

Tamper-evidence and verification:
- Daily signed manifest with SHA256 checksums stored in a separate, access-controlled bucket; verification run weekly and results published to security-dashboard.

Sample Splunk/ES query to find all role changes in last 7 days:
- Splunk: index=audit sourcetype=rbac action IN (create, update, delete) | stats count by actor,action,role | sort - count

4. Data residency and retention rules
Principles:
- Customer data must reside in customer-selected region for Dedicated/Private by default.
- Hosted customers may choose regional residency tiers (US, EU, APAC).
- Minimum retention for logs/telemetry differs by data category and customer contract.

Default retention matrix:
| Data category | Hosted default | Dedicated default | Notes |
|--------------|---------------:|------------------:|-------|
| Audit logs | 365 days | 7 years (enterprise) | Retention configurable per-customer up to 10 years |
| Request traces / traces indexes | 90 days | 365 days | Traces may include PII; redact per policy |
| Billing/cart records | 7 years | 7 years | Required for finance/legal |
| Model artifacts (customer-provided) | customer-selected | customer-selected | Not stored by Redwood unless explicitly requested |

Data residency controls:
- Region tagging at write-time; enforcement via placement policy in object-store gateway.
- Cross-region replication disabled by default for resident datasets unless explicitly authorized and customer-approved.
- KMS keys: customer-managed keys (CMKs) required for Dedicated/Private; hosted uses Redwood-managed keys with optional BYOK.

Retention workflows:
- Automated lifecycle policies enforce deletion/archival.
- For records subject to legal hold, retention state is set to 'legal-hold' and Deletion jobs skip objects with that flag. Legal hold requests require Legal and Security approval.

5. Secure SDLC requirements and gating
Goal: Prevent introduction of vulnerabilities into production through consistent security controls integrated into the software lifecycle.

Mandatory gates (applies to all production-bound changes):
- Threat modeling: required for services that handle customer data or make security-sensitive decisions. Owner: product/security.
- Static analysis (SAST): run on every PR; high and critical findings block merge until fixed or risk-accepted.
- Dependency scanning (OSS): weekly dependency snapshot and CVE triage; critical CVEs must be remediated within 7 days or mitigated with compensating control.
- Secrets scanning: pre-commit hooks + CI step; leaks trigger an automated rotate-and-revoke workflow.
- DAST / staging pentest: quarterly for public endpoints and before every major release for Dedicated/Private.
- Code review: at least one security-aware reviewer for services in scope.
- Security sign-off: Prod deploys require security checklist signed by the service security reviewer.

CI/CD controls:
- Build artifacts signed and stored in artifact registry with immutable tags.
- Deploy pipelines require short-lived deployment tokens issued by OIDC; no static long-lived tokens in CI.
- Canary deployments: default 10% traffic canary for 30 minutes, auto-rollback on error rate > 1% or latency regression > 30%.

6. Incident response (security) procedures
Objective: Provide a repeatable, evidence-preserving and compliant incident response process focused on confidentiality, integrity and availability.

Roles:
- Incident Commander (IC) — coordinates response. Target: Principal Security Engineer on-call.
- Technical Lead — service/infra owner.
- Forensics Lead — handles evidence preservation.
- Communications Lead — external/internal comms.

High-level process (steps):
1) Triage and classification: determine impact, severity (S1-S4), affected tenants, and data exposure.
2) Contain and preserve evidence: isolate affected hosts, capture memory/disk images where applicable, snapshot VMs, and collect relevant logs (see evidence checklist in section 7).
3) Notification: notify Legal, Privacy, Executive team for S1/S2 incidents within 2 hours.
4) Remediation: apply patches, rotate keys, revoke compromised credentials, and deploy mitigations.
5) Post-incident review: 72-hour interim report, full postmortem within 14 days with corrective action plan and owners.

Incident severity criteria (summary):
- S1: Active exfiltration of customer data or production-wide degradation. All hands and exec notification.
- S2: Single-tenant data exposure or significant service outage affecting SLAs. Security + Legal notified.
- S3: Minor outage or security bug with low impact. Triage and fix.
- S4: Informational or near-miss. Document and monitor.

Evidence preservation checklist:
- Capture timestamps, request_ids, user_ids, and request/response payload hashes.
- Preserve raw audit log objects and signed manifests for the relevant time window.
- Export role bindings snapshot and active sessions for scope period.
- Snapshot relevant KMS audit logs, key rotation history (KMS: list-key-rotation-events), and secrets access logs.

Containment commands (examples):
- Revoke Okta sessions: okta sessions invalidate --user <user-id>
- Revoke service tokens: curl -X POST https://auth.internal/v1/tokens/revoke -d '{"token":"<token>"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <admin>'
- Isolate host (k8s): kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data

7. Compliance evidence collection workflows
Purpose: Define how teams produce reproducible evidence for audits (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).

Common evidence artifacts and where to retrieve them:
- RBAC: daily role binding exports (s3://audit-bucket/rbac-snapshots/YYYY-MM-DD.json) and access request tickets (Jira).
- Authentication: Okta sign-on logs export (Splunk saved search), MFA policy screenshots, SCIM provisioning logs.
- Audit logging: Signed manifests, raw objects, index snapshots (Elasticsearch), and delivery pipeline metrics.
- Data residency: object metadata showing region tags, replication configuration, and KMS key ARNs.
- SDLC: CI/CD pipeline run artifacts (build signatures), SAST/DAST reports, threat model docs (Confluence links).
- Incident response: incident timeline exports, forensic images, and remediation evidence (patch commits, rotated keys).

Evidence request workflow (step-by-step):
1) Auditor or internal stakeholder opens an Evidence Request ticket (template) in Jira with scope and desired timeframe.
2) Security Evidence Coordinator reviews and assigns to owner(s) (Service/Platform/Infra).
3) Owners collect artifacts, place them in a short-lived evidence bucket (encrypted) and notify Coordinator.
4) Security validates artifacts against control checklist and produces a signed evidence manifest.
5) Coordinator uploads package to Audit Portal and logs the delivery.

Retention and access controls for evidence bundles:
- Evidence bundles stored for the audit window and archived for 3 years by default (or as contractual).
- Access to evidence bundles is strictly limited to the audit group and security/legal reviewers.

8. Risk and exception process
When to use: Use the risk exception process for temporary deviations where immediate remediation is impractical (e.g., migration dependencies, legacy systems). Exceptions are time-limited and must include compensating controls.

Request process (minimum required fields):
- Owner, affected asset(s), control(s) to be excepted, business justification, risk assessment, compensating controls, proposed TTL (max 90 days), and renewal plan.

Approval criteria and workflow:
1) Submit exception in Jira using the Security Exception template.
2) Security reviews and either: approve (with compensating controls), request more information, or deny.
3) If approved and risk > medium, require Legal and Risk committee sign-off.
4) Exceptions auto-expire and owners receive reminders 14 days before expiry.

Compensating controls examples:
- Network isolations (security groups), strict monitoring + alerting (high-fidelity signatures), shorter retention, and mandatory ticketed remediation steps.

9. Ownership and escalation
Primary owners:
- Security controls and evidence: Priya Nair (Principal Security Engineer).
- RBAC policy engine and provisioning: Platform Security Team (team@redwood.com).
- Audit pipeline and manifests: Observability/Platform Team.

Escalation matrix:
- 0-2 hours: On-call security engineer.
- 2-6 hours: Security Lead and Service Technical Lead.
- 6+ hours or S1 incident: Head of Security and CTO notified.

10. Appendix: sample queries, commands, and templates
- Splunk: index=audit action="role-change" | table _time,actor,role,action,reason
- Elastic: POST /_search {"query":{"bool":{"must":[{"match":{"action":"role-change"}},{"range":{"@timestamp":{"gte":"now-7d"}}}]}}}
- Evidence request Jira template: [Component], [Control ID], [Time window], [Artifacts required], [Owner], [Delivery SLA: 5 business days]
